generation.wrapper: W_s(rank(base)): s = 1 -> rank(base); s > 1 -> decay_linear(rank(base), s)
generation.smoothing_rationale: slow inputs (FINRA short interest levels) keep a plain-rank variant because they move only at dissemination; daily inputs (IV level, slope, change, IV-RV) require decay (tau_k <= 0.70); earnings_drift takes no decay because its base is NaN outside the hold window and a full-window decay would blank it; one size variant because a second decay of a near-constant rank is a duplicate trial
generation.prior_orientation: each new base is written prior-positive (a negative prior is multiplied by -1); the TRAIN rank-IC21 sign fit still orients every candidate

frozen_v2.copy: ids, families, family descriptions, field declarations and DSL bytes identical; dsl_sha256 and lineage rows unchanged

iv_guard.admitted: open interval (0.02, 5); outside it (and at its ends) the cell is NaN before the backfill
iv_guard.backfill: last valid guarded value within 5 sessions (t-4..t), else NaN; never zero
iv_guard.rationale: vendor IV holds garbage (iv_atm_126d member values up to 1.2e16, IV maxima ~69) and is often null; rank after the guard so no single cell dominates; a full-window ts op over sporadic nulls would otherwise blank the name

missing_policy: NaN propagates: a candidate excludes the name that session; no zero fill (the IV backfill carries a past valid value only); earnings_drift is NaN (not zero) without an event in its window

family_fixing.statement: The nine new families, their templates and their window/smoothing grids were declared from published priors in the T8 brief before any v3 measurement; no IC, return, turnover or correlation output of any v3 candidate was consulted. The TRAIN fields manifest was read only for field names, units and coverage. TRAIN fits only per-candidate signs; validation is not used for selection.

family_priors.prior: Intermediate return persistence, with the most recent month excluded.
Path efficiency, return-sign consistency and risk-scaled persistence; related variants share one family budget.
Smoothed contrarian intermediate returns and distance from a trailing mean.
Low volatility, downside variability and volatility expansion; factor preferences, not neutralized alpha.
Raw-dollar liquidity level, expansion and instability; no adjusted-price/share-volume dollar proxy.
Return/flow co-movement and signed dollar-flow balance, using actual shares times raw close.
Adjusted-close position within its own trailing range and slow moving-average structure; no candle fields.
252-session-year proxies only; not calendar seasonality or a claim of independent effects.
Blitz, Huij and Martens (2011, J. Empirical Finance) standardized residual momentum; Grundy and Martin (2001, RFS) factor-adjusted momentum.
Frazzini and Pedersen (2014, JFE) betting against beta; Bollerslev, Li, Patton and Quaedvlieg (2022, JFE) realized semibetas.
Ang, Hodrick, Xing and Zhang (2006, JF) idiosyncratic volatility; Fu (2009, JFE) expected vs unexpected idiosyncratic volatility; Durnev, Morck, Yeung and Zarowin (2003, JAR).
Bali, Cakici and Whitelaw (2011, JFE) MAX; Amaya, Christoffersen, Jacobs and Vasquez (2015, JFE) realized skewness.
Gervais, Kaniel and Mingelgrin (2001, JF) high-volume return premium; Barber and Odean (2008, RFS) attention.
Amihud (2002, J. Financial Markets) unexpected illiquidity; Roll (1984, JF) implied spread; Pastor and Stambaugh (2003, JPE) volume-induced reversal.
Ang and Chen (2002, JFE) asymmetric correlations; Hou and Moskowitz (2005, RFS) price delay; Barberis, Shleifer and Wurgler (2005, JFE).
Baltussen, van Bekkum and van der Grient (2018, JFQA) vol-of-vol; Adrian and Rosenberg (2008, JF) short/long volatility components.
Asquith, Pathak and Ritter (2005, JFE) short interest and institutional ownership; Boehmer, Huszar and Jordan (2010, JFE) the good news in short interest.
family_priors.description: FINRA short interest over lagged shares outstanding, ranked level and smoothed level; high short interest predicts lower returns.
family_priors.prior_sign_meaning: sign of the declared prior on the raw quantity; the DSL base is prior_sign * quantity, so a TRAIN sign of +1 agrees with the prior
family_priors.expected_turnover: very low: inputs move at FINRA dissemination (about every 10.5 sessions); the s1 plain rank steps on those sessions
family_priors.borrow_exposure: high: the prior short leg is high SI/shares_out, and SI/shares_out > 10% is a swap-fin-v1 special-tier flag

family_priors.prior: Hong, Li, Ni, Scheinkman and Yan (2015, working paper) days to cover and stock returns.
family_priors.description: FINRA days to cover (short interest over average daily volume, floored at 1), ranked level and smoothed level; high days to cover predicts lower returns.
family_priors.prior_sign_meaning: sign of the declared prior on the raw quantity; the DSL base is prior_sign * quantity, so a TRAIN sign of +1 agrees with the prior
family_priors.expected_turnover: very low: FINRA cycle updates only; the floor at 1 ties about 40% of rows
family_priors.borrow_exposure: high: the prior short leg is heavily shorted, often small names (SI and mcap flags)

family_priors.prior: Change-in-short-interest prior of the T8 brief, on the short-interest literature of Asquith, Pathak and Ritter (2005, JFE) and Boehmer, Huszar and Jordan (2010, JFE).
family_priors.description: Change in the short-interest ratio over 10, 21 and 42 sessions (about one, two and four FINRA cycles), smoothed; rising short interest predicts lower returns.
family_priors.prior_sign_meaning: sign of the declared prior on the raw quantity; the DSL base is prior_sign * quantity, so a TRAIN sign of +1 agrees with the prior
family_priors.expected_turnover: low: the change refreshes each FINRA cycle; s21 decay spreads each step over a month
family_priors.borrow_exposure: moderate: the short leg is rising short interest, partly already special-tier
family_priors.prior_caveat: the brief pairs ~2 and ~4 FINRA cycles with ~10 and ~21 sessions, but one cycle is ~10.5 sessions; the grid 10/21/42 covers both readings (1, 2 and 4 cycles)

family_priors.prior: Ang, Hodrick, Xing and Zhang (2006, JF) volatility anomaly, implied-volatility analogue.
family_priors.description: Guarded 21-session ATM implied volatility level, ranked and smoothed; high implied volatility predicts lower returns.
family_priors.prior_sign_meaning: sign of the declared prior on the raw quantity; the DSL base is prior_sign * quantity, so a TRAIN sign of +1 agrees with the prior
family_priors.borrow_exposure: moderate: high-IV names skew to small caps and low prices (mcap < $1bn, price < $5, young listings)

family_priors.prior: Vasquez (2017, JFQA) equity volatility term structures; Jiang and Tian-style implied-volatility slope.
family_priors.description: Guarded long-over-short ATM implied volatility ratio (63 or 126 over 21 sessions); an inverted term structure predicts lower returns.
family_priors.prior_sign_meaning: sign of the declared prior on the raw quantity; the DSL base is prior_sign * quantity, so a TRAIN sign of +1 agrees with the prior
family_priors.expected_turnover: low to moderate: daily ratio of two persistent tenors, s21/s63 decay
family_priors.prior_caveat: Vasquez (2017) documents the term-slope effect on option (straddle) returns; the stock-return direction declared in the brief is an extrapolation

family_priors.prior: An, Ang, Bali and Cakici (2014, JF) the joint cross section of stocks and options (ATM approximation).
family_priors.description: Guarded 21-session ATM implied volatility over its value 5 or 21 sessions earlier, smoothed; a sharp implied-volatility rise predicts lower returns.
family_priors.prior_sign_meaning: sign of the declared prior on the raw quantity; the DSL base is prior_sign * quantity, so a TRAIN sign of +1 agrees with the prior
family_priors.expected_turnover: moderate, the fastest v3 family: iv_change_5_s21 is the fastest candidate; decay_linear 21 bounds a white-noise base at lag-1 autocorrelation ~0.93 (Gaussian one-way tau ~0.37), below 0.70
family_priors.prior_caveat: An, Ang, Bali and Cakici (2014) find call-IV increases predict higher and put-IV increases lower stock returns; for ATM (call/put blended) IV the direction is ambiguous a priori; the brief declares rise -> lower

family_priors.prior: Bali and Hovakimian (2009, Management Science) volatility spreads; Goyal and Saretto (2009, JFE) option returns and volatility.
family_priors.description: Guarded 21-session ATM implied volatility minus annualized 21-session realized volatility of daily returns, smoothed; a high spread predicts lower returns.
family_priors.prior_sign_meaning: sign of the declared prior on the raw quantity; the DSL base is prior_sign * quantity, so a TRAIN sign of +1 agrees with the prior
family_priors.expected_turnover: moderate: daily IV and 21-session realized vol, s21/s63 decay
family_priors.borrow_exposure: moderate: high IV-RV spreads concentrate in small, hard-to-borrow names
family_priors.prior_caveat: Bali and Hovakimian (2009), as recalled by the implementer (unverified here), report a negative relation between the realized-minus-implied spread and stock returns, i.e. high IV-RV -> higher returns, opposite to the brief; Goyal and Saretto (2009) concern option returns; the brief sign is kept

family_priors.prior: Chan, Jegadeesh and Lakonishok (1996, JF) momentum strategies; Brandt, Kishore, Santa-Clara and Venkatachalam (2008, working paper) earnings announcement returns.
family_priors.description: Market-relative return summed over vendor-flagged earnings reaction sessions (reaction day and next) within the last 21, 42 or 63 sessions; NaN without an event in the window; positive drift.
family_priors.prior_sign_meaning: sign of the declared prior on the raw quantity; the DSL base is prior_sign * quantity, so a TRAIN sign of +1 agrees with the prior
family_priors.expected_turnover: low: the base is constant between events; names enter on the reaction session and leave after H sessions (about 2/H of the covered names per session; fastest earn_car_21)
family_priors.borrow_exposure: low: shorts are negative-surprise names across sizes

family_priors.prior: Banz (1981, JFE) the size effect.
family_priors.description: Negative log market capitalization, lagged shares outstanding times raw close, ranked; small predicts higher returns (weak; overlaps the logADV63 neutralization).
family_priors.prior_sign_meaning: sign of the declared prior on the raw quantity; the DSL base is prior_sign * quantity, so a TRAIN sign of +1 agrees with the prior
family_priors.expected_turnover: very low: the market-cap rank moves with relative price and lagged share updates, s21 decay
family_priors.borrow_exposure: low if the prior sign holds (shorts big names); high if TRAIN flips the sign (shorts small names)

expected_overlap.rule: pre-measurement prior rank correlations (v2 pairs from review arithmetic; v3 pairs are the implementer priors); not measured, not a selection input; the admission screen culls empirical duplicates

pairs.basis: same [t-125, t-21] formation window; numerators differ by beta*M (sd ~0.05 vs R ~0.25-0.30); denominators differ by residualization (log-sd ~0.1-0.15 vs ~0.45 for the vol level) and 105 vs 126 sessions
log(ivar21/ivar252) = log(var21/var252) + log(1-R2_21) - log(1-R2_252) shares the noisy 21-session variance numerator with -(sd21/sd126); the sign is absorbed by the TRAIN orientation
both are short-over-long variance ratios ending at t with a 252-session denominator
implied and 63-session realized volatility levels rank alike
the spread shares the IV level term
implied and realized volatility changes co-move
days to cover is short interest over volume; the short ratio is over shares

fields.name: close
fields.basis: f64(source float32 raw close) * vendor cumulReturnFactor; adjusted total-return proxy

fields.name: raw_close
fields.basis: unadjusted source float32 close widened to f64; USD/share

fields.name: volume
fields.basis: unadjusted source share volume widened to f64

fields.name: mkt_ret
fields.basis: equal-weight mean adjusted close-to-close return (close[d] / close[d-1] - 1) over the previous session's (d-1) as-of members, broadcast to every name present at d; produced upstream, not by the DSL

fields.name: si_shares
fields.basis: FINRA consolidated shares short (currentShortPositionQuantity); as-of: latest row with available_at (the official dissemination date) strictly before date(session), NaN when older than 45 calendar days; produced upstream

fields.name: si_dtc
fields.basis: FINRA days to cover (daysToCoverQuantity, floored at 1.00 by FINRA); same as-of clock and 45-day staleness as si_shares

fields.name: iv_atm_21d
fields.basis: vendor ATM implied volatility, annualized decimal (0.30 = 30%), 21-session constant maturity, earnings-adjusted clean IV; same-date end-of-day vendor row, known at the session close mark; null, non-finite or <= 0 -> NaN; vendor garbage remains (values far above 5), so candidates guard it

fields.name: earn_recent
fields.basis: indicator: 1 on the vendor earnings price-reaction session (earnFlag 0) and the session after (earnFlag 1), 0 otherwise (N and -1); same-date vendor row, known at the session close mark; NaN when the vendor row is absent

fields.name: shares_out
fields.basis: vendor shares outstanding (thousands x 1000) of the last line row dated <= date(session) - 90 calendar days (A8 lag), restated to the session share basis by the cumulReturnFactor ratio; NaN when that row is older than 490 days

data.decision_support: as-of member AND present AND finite positive current close
data.vm_support: full historical as-of membership; temporal raw history retained
data.forward_support: strict source presence and positive finite endpoints; pair counts and missing fractions reported
data.market_return: mkt_ret panel field: equal-weight mean adjusted close-to-close return (close[d] / close[d-1] - 1) over the previous session's (d-1) as-of members, broadcast to every name present at d; produced upstream, not by the DSL
data.prior_bar_accounting: prior_bars charges mkt_ret one prior bar (d-1..d), the same as ret; native_prior_bars follows the native typecheck, which charges fields 0

field_clocks.si_shares: finra-asof: available_at (official dissemination date) < date(session), strict; age > 45 calendar days -> NaN
field_clocks.si_dtc: finra-asof: available_at (official dissemination date) < date(session), strict; age > 45 calendar days -> NaN
field_clocks.iv_atm_21d: vendor end-of-day row dated the session; known at the session close mark (the close clock)
field_clocks.iv_atm_63d: vendor end-of-day row dated the session; known at the session close mark (the close clock)
field_clocks.iv_atm_126d: vendor end-of-day row dated the session; known at the session close mark (the close clock)
field_clocks.earn_recent: vendor end-of-day row dated the session; flags the reaction session (event public by its close) and the next
field_clocks.shares_out: A8: vendor share count dated <= date(session) - 90 calendar days, restated by the session factor

data.causality: row d of a signal uses fields known by the session-d close mark (the v2 close clock) and is scored against returns after d; si_* are strictly before date(d); shares_out lags 90 days
data.short_interest_ratio: si_shares / shares_out; a split between the FINRA settlement and the session misstates it by the split factor until the next dissemination
data.short_interest_change: si_change_10 spans about one FINRA cycle: on sessions with no dissemination in (t-10, t] the change is zero for most names (tied ranks) and the s21 decay carries the previous cycle
vendor_caveats: iv_atm_*: vendor clean IV removes the earnings effect with the vendor earnings calendar (forward-looking by construction; calendar vintage unproven); no vintage proof
earn_recent: vendor calendar vintage unproven; the reaction session is public by its close
si_*: settlements before 2021-06 come from a later FINRA consolidated republication
data.size: shares_out * raw_close (USD); mktcap_lagged is not used (about 75% member coverage vs 99.7%)
data.earnings_window: earn_recent flags the reaction session and the next; the event return is earn_recent * (ret - mkt_ret) summed over the hold window
data.realized_vol: stddev(ret, 21) * 15.874507866387544 (sqrt 252), annualized decimal like the IV fields
data.unused_field_reasons: mktcap_lagged/size_grp: lower coverage than shares_out * raw_close; is_common: static, not point-in-time

orientation.inverse: multiply centered rank by frozen sign

composition.diversity: structural economic-family/template budgets; no statistical independence claim
composition.storage: one D*N blend plus one incoming candidate; orient then accumulate before discarding candidate (one VM pass)

planned_turnover.desired_transform: centered tied rank; dollar-neutral; gross1; no winsorization
planned_turnover.membership_exit: force planned zero immediately; do not renormalize remaining names
report: initial deployment included and separately disclosed
planned_turnover.interpretation: planned weight change only; no execution, price drift, fees, borrow, liquidity caps, Sharpe or capacity claim

trials.reruns: retain attempts; v1/v2 attempts remain prior trials of the reused 96

static_validation.rule: python re-parse: canonical round-trip, registry arity, declared fields, positive integer windows, lookback recomputed per typecheck, dag slot bound
static_validation.slot_estimate: post-order interning and refcount retirement; native --plan-only authoritative
